searchDocs.title: RATE​
searchDocs.content: </> Nerp.RATE: number Sample spacing the delay is measured in so 20 matches robloxs physics properly

searchDocs.title: DELAY​
searchDocs.content: </> Nerp.DELAY: DelayPreset Default delay preset. "SMOOTH" is two samples of intervals

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Nerp.new( rate: number,-- Sample spacing in seconds. Default to 20 when nil delay: DelayPreset-- "SMOOTH" or "LOW_LATENCY". Defaults to "SMOOTH" ) → Store Creates a store Thee store holds every tracked target, so the render clock and the PreRender connection. One store per client is enough for most games. local store = Nerp.new(20, "SMOOTH")

searchDocs.title: Server part​
searchDocs.content: local now = Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() local cf = CFrame.new(Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * RADIUS, 6, math.sin(angle) * RADIUS)) withoutNerp.CFrame = cf remote:FireAllClients(now, cf)

searchDocs.title: Client part​
searchDocs.content: local store = Nerp.new(20, "LOW_LATENCY") -- OR "SMOOTH" store:track(withNerp) store:start() remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(t, ct) store:feed(withNerp:GetFullName(), { { t = t, ct = ct } }) end)   The ID has to match, track keeys on GetFullName() so a feed that sends part.Name is ignored.

searchDocs.title: Install​
searchDocs.content: [dependencies] Nerp = "superdupernairobi/nerp@0.1.0"   Studio users: grab Nerp.rbxm from the latest release and put it in ReplicatedStorage.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: local Nerp = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Nerp) local store = Nerp.new(20, "SMOOTH") -- OR LOW_LATENCY store:track(workspace.with_nerp) store:start() remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(t, cf) store:feed(workspace.with_nerp:GetFullName(), { { t = t, cf = cf } }) end)   The delay is a multiple and not a time  "SMOOTH" is two samples of intervals, "LOW_LATENCY" is one and a half, so, at 20Hz that is 100ms and 75ms. Basically, two intervals leaves one whole sample of slack, so a single late packet still has a pair to interpolate between. At one interval the clock sits on the newest sample and any jitter pushes it past the end, which is where extrapolation starts. LOW_LATENCY is the one that can extrapolate, so it is for close combat and not for vehicles.

searchDocs.title: What to feed it​
searchDocs.content: One sample is { t: number, cf: CFrame }, t is a server held timestamp, it uses Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() which is the obvious source. Feed thee ID you tracked, which is inst:GetFullName()

searchDocs.title: Stats​
searchDocs.content: store:stats() returns counts for the last frame, which is: targets, applied, held, stale, plus renderTime, newest and delay. applied and held should sum to targets, when held climbs, the buffer has nothing to interpolate between at the render time, which usually means the feed key does not match the tracked id.
